div.head: Af El. 49.10
div.ab: Ic ða Ælfred Westseaxna cyning eallum minum witum þas geeowde, ⁊ hie ða cwædon, þæt him þæt licode eallum to healdanne.
Ic þa Ælfred Westseaxena cyng eallum minum witum þas geowde, ⁊ hy þa cwædon, þæt heom þæt licode eallum wel to healdene.
Ego Ælfredus Westsaxonum rex omnibus sapientibus meis hęc ostendi, et dixerunt omnes: ‘Placet ea custodire’.
Ic ða Ælfred Westseaxna cyning eallum minnum witum þas geeowde, ⁊ hie ða cwædon, þæt him þæt licode eallum to healdanne.
Ich nun, Aelfred, König der Westsachsen, zeigte diese [folgenden Gesetze] allen meinen Witan, und sie erklärten darauf, dass es ihnen allen gefiele, [sie] zu halten.
I, then, Alfred, king of the West Saxons, showed these [following laws] to all my councillors, and they then declared that it pleased them all to keep [them].
I, then, Alfred, King of the West Saxons, have shewn these to all my councillors, and they have declared that it met with the approval of all, that they should be observed.
Then I, Alfred, king of the West Saxons, showed these to all my councillors, and they then said that they were all pleased to observe them.
I, Alfred, king of the West Saxons, then presented these [rulings] to all my counselors, and they then said, that it pleased them all to hold [them].

Vgl. Gl Königstitel 4a; ‘Westsachsen’ auch im Testament Ælfreds (Bi 553); a. 878 *Bi 545; in Bi 581 nur Rubrik; er heisst 875 so in Bi 539. Meist nennt er sich ‘König’ schlechthin oder voller rex Anglorum et Saxonum (Bi 561. *571; vgl. Stubbs Will. Malm. II p. xliv; et fehlt Bi 564. 581) oder Angulsaxonum (Bi 565; Angol Sa. 567f.) oder Saxonum allein (noch a. 898 Bi 550. 576), was alles ‘Angelsachsen’ bedeutet. Er wird angeredet rex Anglorum (Bi 555; *563 ist verfälscht); er selbst nennt sich nicht so

Cf. Gl Königstitel 4a; ‘West Saxons’ also in Ælfred’s will (Bi 553); a. 878 *Bi 545; in Bi 581 only in the rubric; he is so called in 875 in Bi 539. Usually he calls himself simply ‘king’, or more fully rex Anglorum et Saxonum (Bi 561. *571; cf. Stubbs Will. Malm. II p. xliv; et is lacking in Bi 564. 581), or Angulsaxonum (Bi 565; Angol Sa. 567f.), or Saxonum alone (still in 898, Bi 550. 576), all of which mean ‘Anglo-Saxons’. He is addressed as rex Anglorum (Bi 555; *563 is falsified); he does not call himself so
